## 1. Where this belongs, and why here

The map's row for the numeric tower sends every prelude question to §4.2-4.3 of `explorations/coordinator/map/spec-to-implementation.md` (`spec-to-implementation.md:323`), whose table of the compiler prelude says `RR64` is "present, **flat**: … with `+`, `-`, `/`, `juxtaposition`, `DOT`, `^`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `SQRT` and the comparisons all declared on the trait itself (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:412-441`)" (`spec-to-implementation.md:411`).

So the declaration site is `trait RR64` in `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi` and its body in `.fss`, and the same map says operator and functional-method declarations inside a compiler-prelude trait are the established shape, not an invention: "**yes** — the compiler prelude declares its own operators this way (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:412-441`)" (`spec-to-implementation.md:356`).

The native side is equally settled: the compiler world's one Java-interop mechanism is `import java` over `nativeHelpers/`, read by `ForeignJava` with ASM and wrapped by `FortressTransformer` into `nativewrapper_cache` (`explorations/coordinator/map/modules-and-phases.md:441-449`, and the divergence table at `:483`, "Natives | `builtinPrimitive` + `interpreter/glue/` | `import java` + `nativeHelpers/` + `nativeInterface/`"); `spec-to-implementation.md:157` records the same for the feature row "foreign import".

Nothing about this rung touches a phase: the names are missing from the prelude, so every blocked file dies in disambiguation with `Variable <name> is not defined` (`explorations/compile-ladder/after/raw/tests/buffons.fss.compile` and six more), which is a library gap and not a checker or codegen gap. There is no phase already doing this work, which is the trap rung 7 fell into (`compiler/phases/PhaseOrder.java:57,142`); the one phase that could have interfered, `INTEGERLITERALFOLDING`, folds integer literals only and none of the thirteen deals in one.

## 2. Precedent search: has the team solved this here, and in how many ways

Four ways, and they do not agree. This matters, because the answer decides the return types.

**(a) The interpreter's api, on `trait Number`.** `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:319-332` declares `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan`, `atan2(self, x: Number)`, `log`, `exp`, `floor` and `ceiling` returning `RR64`, the two enclosing operators `opr |\self/|` and `opr |/self\|` returning `ZZ64`, and `truncate` returning `ZZ64`. `round` is **not** in this api at all.

**(b) The interpreter's bodies, twice.** `trait Number` gives all thirteen a default body that forwards to `asFloat(self)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:405-419`), and `value object Float` binds each one to a `builtinPrimitive` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:162-190`), including the `round(self): ZZ64` that the api omits (`:189-190`). The glue is `java.lang.Math`, one method each, in `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Float.java:318-386`.

**(c) The interpreter's `trait QQ`, which follows the specification where (a) and (b) do not.** `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:396-401` declares `floor`, `ceiling`, `truncate` and `round` on ℚ returning `ZZ` — the specification's ℤ — and `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:589` gives `round` a hand-written round-half-to-even body. That body is the precedent this rung follows for `round`.

**(d) The team's own draft for the compiler world**, commented out in the file being edited: `ceiling(self):RR64` and `floor(self):RR64` at `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:439-440`, with both natives already bound (`simpleDoubleArith.doubleFloor => jDoubleFloor`, `doubleCeiling => jDoubleCeiling`, `CompilerBuiltin.fss:212-213`) and already used by the enclosing operators of the same trait at `.fss:898-899`. Those two enclosing operators return `RR64` in the compiler world (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:437-438`), where the interpreter's return `ZZ64`.

The in-file shape copied for the body is `opr SQRT(self): RR64 = jDoubleSQRT(self)` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:900`, pre-edit), with its native bound in the `import java` block at `.fss:196-214`.

No corpus file competes for any of the thirteen names. `grep -rnE "(sin|cos|tan|asin|acos|atan|atan2|log|exp|floor|ceiling|truncate|round)[[:space:]]*\([[:space:]]*self"` over `ProjectFortress/tests` and every `*_tests/` directory returns nothing, and a declaration-shaped grep over the same eight directories returns only uses. This is the check rung 1 lost a cycle to (`library_tests/MaybeTest9.fss`'s own `trait Equality`); it is clean here. The one place the names are declared again is the target program itself, at the array level and deliberately overloaded with the scalar: `exp[\T extends Number, I\](a: Array[\T,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](exp)` (`explorations/apl/mg/FlatArrays2.fss:44-45`), which is why the scalar must be a functional method nameable as a bare `exp`.

## 3. The specification, read

`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex` is chapter 33, "Numbers", and it has exactly one section, "Rational Numbers" (`:12-17`); the ℝ types appear in it only as names inside the subtype lists of the ℚ family (`:37-90`). The four rounding methods are declared at `:457-462` and defined in prose at `:464-477`: `floor` "returns the largest integer that is not greater", `ceiling` "the smallest integer that is not less", `round` "returns the integer that is closest … but if this rational number is exactly halfway between two consecutive integers, then `round` returns whichever of the two integers is **even**", `truncate` "returns the ceiling … if it is negative, and otherwise … the floor", that is toward zero. `:464` and `:467` both say "likewise the enclosing operator", so the specification makes the named method and the bracket the same operation with the same result type.

**A correction to the brief.** CLIMB-BATCH-1.md section F says "the 'Real' numbers section of that chapter is commented out (`numbers.tex:920`)". There is no such section and no such line: the file is 566 lines long and has no second section, commented out or otherwise, and no file under `Specification/basic-lib` or `Specification/advanced-lib` reaches line 920 except `advanced-lib/binary.tex`. The chapter's many `%` lines are the ASCII sources of the typeset displays, as `explorations/coordinator/map/design-intent-sources.md:104` already records for `algebraic-constraints.tex`; they are not disabled text. The conclusion the brief drew from the wrong citation is nevertheless right — the specification has no chapter for the real types — but it is right because the chapter was never written, not because it was switched off.

For `exp`, `log` and the trigonometric functions the prose is silent in the sense that matters (no definition and no declaration), but it is not silent about their existence, and two passages are worth having on the record because they are the closest the prose comes: `Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:123-133` lists "`+`, `-`, `×`, `·`, `/`, `!`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `√`, `floor`, `ceiling`, `hyperfloor`, `hyperceiling`, `gcd`, `lcm`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `arcsin`, `arccos`, `arctan`" as the operations that may combine numeric **static** expressions — naming six of the transcendentals in mathematical spelling (`arcsin`, not `asin`), defining none, and not naming `exp`, `log` or `atan2` at all; and `Specification/basic/dimensions.tex:214-215` presumes them as library functions — "Other numerical functions, such as `sin` and `log`, require dimensionless arguments."

Neither passage constrains a return type or an argument type, so for the nine non-rounding methods the precedent of section 2 governs, as the brief says.

**Rule 3 in passing.** Rows 314 and 316 of the gap ledger, and the comment at `ProjectFortress/library_tests/IntLiteralArithRung7.fss:30-31`, cite `Specification/library/apis/FortressLibrary.tex`, `…/CompilerLibrary.tex` and `…/CompilerBuiltin.tex`. That directory does not exist in this repository: the api renderings are `\input` files generated from the `.fsi` sources at spec-build time (`Specification/library/default-libraries.tex:27,39`), and the two `Compiler*` ones are not even among the inputs the spec build names. So an `(api listing)` citation under `Specification/library/apis/` is not merely circular in the sense of `Specification/library/structure.tex:25-31`; it cites a path that is not in the tree and cannot be opened. This rung cites no such path.

## 4. The four deviations, each a decision

**(i) `floor` and `ceiling` return `RR64`, where the specification says ℤ.** Alternatives: `RR64`, which is precedent (d) — the team's commented-out draft in this very file — and also precedent (a), the interpreter's method type; or `ZZ64`, which is the specification's ℤ and the interpreter's *bracket* type. `RR64` was chosen. The reason is not that the specification is silent; it is that the specification requires the method and its enclosing operator to be the same operation with the same result (`numbers.tex:464`, `:467`, "likewise the enclosing operator"), the compiler prelude's two brackets are already declared `RR64` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:437-438`), and changing a declared type the prelude already has is one of the two stops CLIMB-BATCH-1.md reserves. Declaring the methods `ZZ64` would have satisfied the specification's magnitude and broken its identity, leaving one trait in which `floor(x)` and `⌊x⌋` have different types. Declaring them `RR64` keeps the trait coherent and leaves a single pre-existing deviation, now written down as a ledger row rather than doubled.

**(ii) `round` and `truncate` return `ZZ64`.** No enclosing operator for either exists in the compiler prelude, so (i)'s constraint does not apply; `ZZ64` is both the precedent (`FortressBuiltin.fss:187-190`) and an integer type, which is what ℤ asks for. The alternative, `RR64` for symmetry with `floor` and `ceiling`, was rejected: it would deviate from the specification and from the precedent at once, for symmetry alone.

**(iii) `round` is built on `Math.rint`, not `Math.round`.** `Math.round` rounds an exact half toward positive infinity, which contradicts `numbers.tex:470-472`; `Math.rint` rounds an exact half to the even integer, which is that sentence. The interpreter's `Float$Round` is `Math.round(x)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Float.java:382-385`), so this is a deliberate deviation from precedent (b) — taken because precedent (c), the team's own ℚ body at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:589`, implements the specification's rule in Fortress, and because a gated interpreter test asserts it: `ProjectFortress/tests/RationalTest.fss:428` asserts `round(15/6) = 2`, that is `round(2.5) = 2`. The differential in section 6 shows `walk` answering `3` for the same value at `RR64`. Ledger row (provisional 329) carries the interpreter-side defect.

**(iv) `atan2` takes `x: RR64` where the interpreter takes `x: Number`.** The compiler world's `Number` is an empty marker (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:96`, `spec-to-implementation.md:410`) and carries no arithmetic, and every binary declaration in the compiler world's `trait RR64` narrows the interpreter's `Number` parameter to `RR64` already (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:419-435` against `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:291-316`). So the type follows the file. The parameter **name** `x` is kept from the interpreter rather than renamed to the file's usual `other`, because for `atan2` the name carries meaning: `self` is the *y* coordinate and the argument is the *x* coordinate, which is what `Float.java:334-337` computes (`ATan2 extends RR2R`, `f(y, x) = Math.atan2(y, x)`, with `RR2R.applyMethod(FObject x, FValue y)` at `:86-92` putting `self` first).

**A fifth decision, about the natives' home.** The eleven new static methods went into `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleDoubleArith.java`, the team's own file, rather than into a new file beside it as rung 7 did with `simpleIntLiteralArith.java`. The criterion is the one that made rung 7 split: its helper dealt in a Fortress type and needed a clause in `NamingCzar.fortressTypeForForeignJavaType` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:341-343`). These eleven deal in `double` and `long`, which the generic path maps without a clause (`NamingCzar.java:441-446`, `s(Type.LONG_TYPE, fortLib, "ZZ64")` and `s(Type.DOUBLE_TYPE, fortLib, "RR64")`), and they are the same kind of one-line wrapper over `java.lang.Math` as the file's existing `doublePow`, `doubleSQRT`, `doubleFloor`, `doubleCeiling` and `doubleAbs`. A new file would have split the double primitives across two files with no criterion. Worth noting for the next rung that touches this: `doubleTruncate` and `doubleRound` are the first natives in the tree that take a `double` and return a `long`.

**A sixth decision, about the test's assertions.** The comparing `assert` has no `RR64` form — rung 4 added `ZZ32`, `String` and `Character` only (`Library/CompilerLibrary.fsi:45-49`) — and this rung did not add one. The alternative, adding `assert(x: RR64, y: RR64)` and `assert(x: RR64, y: RR64, failMsg: String)` to `CompilerLibrary`, was rejected for two reasons: rung T of this batch is editing `CompilerLibrary` in the same wave, and batch rule 1 keeps the merge clean by keeping the rungs' declarations disjoint; and floating-point assertions want an epsilon rather than `=`, which a comparing `assert` cannot express. The test therefore uses the Boolean form over `opr =` for the exact cases and over a local `near` for the inexact ones, and `.asZZ32` into rung 4's `ZZ32` form for `round` and `truncate` — the same idiom as `ProjectFortress/library_tests/IntLiteralArithRung7.fss:58-70`.

The chapter's many `%` lines are the ASCII sources of the typeset displays, as `explorations/coordinator/map/design-intent-sources.md:104` already records for `algebraic-constraints.tex`; they are not disabled text. The conclusion the brief drew from the wrong citation is nevertheless right — the specification has no chapter for the real types — but it is right because the chapter was never written, not because it was switched off.

For `exp`, `log` and the trigonometric functions the prose is silent in the sense that matters (no definition and no declaration), but it is not silent about their existence, and two passages are worth having on the record because they are the closest the prose comes: `Specification/basic/expressions/constant.tex:123-133` lists "`+`, `-`, `×`, `·`, `/`, `!`, `MIN`, `MAX`, `√`, `floor`, `ceiling`, `hyperfloor`, `hyperceiling`, `gcd`, `lcm`, `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `arcsin`, `arccos`, `arctan`" as the operations that may combine numeric **static** expressions — naming six of the transcendentals in mathematical spelling (`arcsin`, not `asin`), defining none, and not naming `exp`, `log` or `atan2` at all; and `Specification/basic/dimensions.tex:214-215` presumes them as library functions — "Other numerical functions, such as `sin` and `log`, require dimensionless arguments."

Neither passage constrains a return type or an argument type, so for the nine non-rounding methods the precedent of section 2 governs, as the brief says.

**Rule 3 in passing.** Rows 314 and 316 of the gap ledger, and the comment at `ProjectFortress/library_tests/IntLiteralArithRung7.fss:30-31`, cite `Specification/library/apis/FortressLibrary.tex`, `…/CompilerLibrary.tex` and `…/CompilerBuiltin.tex`. That directory does not exist in this repository: the api renderings are `\input` files generated from the `.fsi` sources at spec-build time (`Specification/library/default-libraries.tex:27,39`), and the two `Compiler*` ones are not even among the inputs the spec build names. So an `(api listing)` citation under `Specification/library/apis/` is not merely circular in the sense of `Specification/library/structure.tex:25-31`; it cites a path that is not in the tree and cannot be opened. This rung cites no such path.

## 4. The four deviations, each a decision

**(i) `floor` and `ceiling` return `RR64`, where the specification says ℤ.** Alternatives: `RR64`, which is precedent (d) — the team's commented-out draft in this very file — and also precedent (a), the interpreter's method type; or `ZZ64`, which is the specification's ℤ and the interpreter's *bracket* type. `RR64` was chosen. The reason is not that the specification is silent; it is that the specification requires the method and its enclosing operator to be the same operation with the same result (`numbers.tex:464`, `:467`, "likewise the enclosing operator"), the compiler prelude's two brackets are already declared `RR64` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:437-438`), and changing a declared type the prelude already has is one of the two stops CLIMB-BATCH-1.md reserves. Declaring the methods `ZZ64` would have satisfied the specification's magnitude and broken its identity, leaving one trait in which `floor(x)` and `⌊x⌋` have different types. Declaring them `RR64` keeps the trait coherent and leaves a single pre-existing deviation, now written down as a ledger row rather than doubled.

**(ii) `round` and `truncate` return `ZZ64`.** No enclosing operator for either exists in the compiler prelude, so (i)'s constraint does not apply; `ZZ64` is both the precedent (`FortressBuiltin.fss:187-190`) and an integer type, which is what ℤ asks for. The alternative, `RR64` for symmetry with `floor` and `ceiling`, was rejected: it would deviate from the specification and from the precedent at once, for symmetry alone.

**(iii) `round` is built on `Math.rint`, not `Math.round`.** `Math.round` rounds an exact half toward positive infinity, which contradicts `numbers.tex:470-472`; `Math.rint` rounds an exact half to the even integer, which is that sentence. The interpreter's `Float$Round` is `Math.round(x)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Float.java:382-385`), so this is a deliberate deviation from precedent (b) — taken because precedent (c), the team's own ℚ body at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:589`, implements the specification's rule in Fortress, and because a gated interpreter test asserts it: `ProjectFortress/tests/RationalTest.fss:428` asserts `round(15/6) = 2`, that is `round(2.5) = 2`. The differential in section 6 shows `walk` answering `3` for the same value at `RR64`. Ledger row (provisional 329) carries the interpreter-side defect.

**(iv) `atan2` takes `x: RR64` where the interpreter takes `x: Number`.** The compiler world's `Number` is an empty marker (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:96`, `spec-to-implementation.md:410`) and carries no arithmetic, and every binary declaration in the compiler world's `trait RR64` narrows the interpreter's `Number` parameter to `RR64` already (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:419-435` against `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:291-316`). So the type follows the file. The parameter **name** `x` is kept from the interpreter rather than renamed to the file's usual `other`, because for `atan2` the name carries meaning: `self` is the *y* coordinate and the argument is the *x* coordinate, which is what `Float.java:334-337` computes (`ATan2 extends RR2R`, `f(y, x) = Math.atan2(y, x)`, with `RR2R.applyMethod(FObject x, FValue y)` at `:86-92` putting `self` first).

39:- **The eight-rung climb took 8h37m and every minute of it was serial**: 36 agents, no two ever overlapping, the sum of agent walls plus the 35 inter-agent gaps equalling the span exactly. 55:- Behind that wall the type checker does not know templates: there is no `TemplateGap`/`_SyntaxTransformation` case anywhere under `scala_src/typechecker/`. The implementation class `F*` works only for the types that are in `NamingCzar`'s `specialFortressDescriptors` table (`:508-532`: `ZZ32`, `Character`, `ZZ`, `ZZ32Vector`); for any other type a helper declared over `F*` compiles clean and then fails to link with `NoSuchMethodError`, because the generated wrapper in `nativewrapper_cache` mirrors the Java signature while the emitted call site uses the interface descriptor. Two operational notes from the same probe: a `fortress compile` whose source file has not changed writes nothing and exits 0, and a change to a helper's signature leaves a stale class in `default_repository/caches/nativewrapper_cache` that must be deleted or the old signature is what the run links against.

Through a declared binding the divergence predates rung 6 -- `a: ZZ64 = 4294967295`, `b: ZZ64 = 5`, walk `false`, compiled `true`, by way of `ZZ64.coerce(x: IntLiteral) = x.asZZ64` (`CompilerBuiltin.fss:557`) -- so annotating the binding is not a workaround and none is known; through an undeclared binding it is what rung 6 opened, where the stub threw before. No library edit repairs it, `asZZ` included, because the wrap precedes every getter; the repair is in `forIntLiteralExpr`, whose decimal-string branch does not wrap and whose two narrow branches need the signed range rather than `bitLength`. Same class as row 79, the silent compiled-against-interpreter disagreement, reached through the literal's value instead of `typecase`. Rung 7 widened it from comparison to arithmetic: `a = 4294967295`, `b = 1`, `println (a + b)` gives walk `4294967296` and compiled `0` (`compile-ladder/rung7/probes/p39.fss`). **Repaired by R2 of the repair batch** (the rung's work of 2026-09-18, landed on `main` 2026-09-19 as `6a63980b`), whose entries below state what the compiled path does now; this bullet describes the tree up to `49ee5e91`.
100:- **Repair R1 of the repair batch, a top-level mutable variable in the transaction, landed** (2026-09-19, `42d51c47`, `compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/REPORT.md`): a mutable variable declared at the top level of a component is stored in a transactional cell on the compiled path: its singleton field is `ACC_FINAL` and holds a `MutableFValue`, reads and writes route through `Transaction.TXRead`/`TXWrite` while a transaction is running, and a nested code-generation context captures the cell rather than a copy of the value (`VarCodeGen.MutableStaticBinding`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/VarCodeGen.java:310-399`; `CodeGen.java:5873-5907`, `:4648-4651`, `:5909-5951`). Rung 3 (`4d419c9e8`) had emitted a bare `GETSTATIC`/`PUTSTATIC` on a non-final field, so such a variable was outside the transaction that `atomic do … end` really does start — against `Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:38-42` — and a write from inside a `for` body or a parallel `do … also` arm was lost outright, at one thread as well as at four. # R1: the record

## FACTS.md

Five lines. The first is the rung; the next three are facts it established on the way; the
fifth is the repair round.

> A mutable variable declared at the top level of a component is stored in a transactional cell on the compiled path: its singleton field is `ACC_FINAL` and holds a `MutableFValue`, reads and writes route through `Transaction.TXRead`/`TXWrite` while a transaction is running, and a nested code-generation context captures the cell rather than a copy of the value (`VarCodeGen.MutableStaticBinding`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/VarCodeGen.java:310-399`; `CodeGen.java:5872-5906`, `:4647-4650`, `:5908-5951`). Rung 3 (`4d419c9e8`) had emitted a bare `GETSTATIC`/`PUTSTATIC` on a non-final field, so such a variable was outside the transaction that `atomic do … end` really does start — against `Specification/basic/expressions/atomic.tex:38-42` — and a write from inside a `for` body or a parallel `do … also` arm was lost outright, at one thread as well as at four. Repaired 2026-09-19 by R1 of the repair batch; gated by `compiler_tests/MutableTopLevelVarInLoop` and `AtomicTopLevelObjectVar`, both deterministic and both failing at one thread on the tree each of them guards, and by `compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevelVar` under contention. **The bound**: this is `atomic` in a function body or a loop body. As the trailing expression of a `do … also` arm the generated class does not verify at all, before the repair or after (`VerifyError: Inconsistent stackmap frames`, ledger row 322), so "a top-level mutable variable is in the transaction" must not be read as "`atomic` on a top-level mutable variable works". Three defects the rung repairs beyond its own subject, each measured on the base tree and after: a top-level mutable variable assigned from inside an `fn` expression body was silently lost (`probes/skeptic/SK2Closure.fss`: base `g = 0`, landed `g = 7`); a *local* mutable variable of type `String` assigned inside `atomic` failed the verifier (`SK16LocalString.fss`: base `VerifyError: Bad type on operand stack`, landed `st = a b`); and a two-location invariant inside one transaction now holds under contention (`SK8Swap.fss`: base at four threads `x = 9692 y = -8877 sum = 815` against an invariant of 1000, landed PASS).

> **The gate's thread count is inherited from the shell, and this repository pins it to one.** The chain is: the `fastTrack` macro that runs `compiler_tests` sets `FORTRESS_CACHES` and no thread count and no `newenvironment` (`build.xml:927-953`), so the forked JUnit JVM inherits the ambient environment; the harness runs each program in a further subprocess that inherits again (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/tests/unit_tests/FileTests.java:480-486`); and `FortressExecutable.getNumThreads` reads `FORTRESS_THREADS` first and only falls back to the processor count or `floor(n/2)` when it is unset (`:37-44`). `experiment/env.sh:6` exports `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, every rung brief tells the agent to source it, and `explorations/coordinator/iteration-cost.md:126` records that no run in the climb used anything else — so in the gate as this project runs it, `compiler_tests` gets one worker. Measured consequence: `compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevelVar` passes on the *unrepaired* base tree at one thread (`compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/skeptic/skeptic-basetree.txt`, `BASE run AtomicTopLevelVar THREADS=1 :: PASS`), so it is vacuous there and the two deterministic tests are what carry R1. The `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` in the `testSystem` shards (`build.xml:1184`) is a second, explicit pin on a corpus this does not concern. A concurrency defect on the compiled path is therefore **not** gateable by a concurrent test as the gate stands; it is gateable only by a test that fails at one thread. (This line replaces the claim R1 first offered, that `compiler_tests` runs with more than one worker: the chain was right as far as it went and stopped one line short of `getNumThreads`'s first statement.)

> `run_out_WIcontains` is not implemented by the test harness. `FileTests.generalTestFailed` implements six checks — `_contains` (`FileTests.java:147`), `_does_not_contain` (`:155`), `_matches` (`:163`), `_WImatches` (`:171`), `_WCIequals` (`:180`) and `_equals` (`:190`) — and no `_WIcontains` among them, so the sixteen `.test` files that still use it assert only the default "stdout contains pass or PASS" that applies when no check matched (`FileTests.java:266-272`). Nothing is silently unchecked, but the line does nothing. Eight of the sixteen are the last climb's own new tests, because the rung briefs name `library_tests/Boolean.test` as the format to copy and that file carries the inert line; the next brief should name a file that does not. R1's three tests use `run_out_contains=PASS` and `run_out_does_not_contain=FAIL`, the form fifteen `.test` files already used.

> The compiled world's mutable-variable cell holds `fortress.AnyType.Any`, the language's top type, not `runtimeValues.FValue`: `FValue` is an abstract class (`runtimeValues/FValue.java:13`) and a compiled closure is not one of its subclasses, so a mutable variable of arrow type failed the verifier. The defect was already in the tree for *local* mutable variables, which have always been stored in such a cell (`compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/P15LocalArrow.fss`, `P16LocalArrowTask.fss`: `VerifyError` on `49ee5e91`, `f(1) = 3` after R1), and R1 fixed both kinds by widening the payload (`runtimeValues/MutableFValue.java:18-32`, `runtimeSystem/Transaction.java:20,27-28,144,152,226`).

> **The transaction runtime built twenty-two of its twenty-three disabled debug messages eagerly, and on the transactional path that was a crash, not only a cost.** `Transaction.java` has fourteen `debug(` call sites and `BaseTask.java` nine; each concatenated its argument before `debug(String)` tested the flag, except `BaseTask.java:248`, which rung 0 of this same climb had already guarded. Nine of `Transaction.java`'s sites stringify a Fortress value or a table of them, which for an object or trait value with no `asString` of its own enters the `FValue.toString` / `CompilerBuiltin.fss:338` / `stringOps.java:38-40` cycle (ledger row 321) and overflows the stack. Once R1 routed a top-level mutable variable's accesses through the transaction, a twelve-line single-threaded program that ran on `49ee5e91` died (`probes/skeptic/SK25ObjNoAtomicVsAtomic.fss`, frames in `sk25-recursion-entry.txt`). All twenty-three call sites now carry the `if (debug)` guard, twenty-two of them applied in R1's repair round (2026-09-19) in the idiom `BaseTask.java:248` already used, and the case is gated by `compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevelObjectVar`, whose object type deliberately declares no `asString`. The per-access cost this removes is the mechanism ledger row 302 measured at about 34 % of a 156× gap: inside a transaction each read and write had been building a discarded string of the value (`Transaction.java:162,166,227`), each commit rendering both hash tables (`:232`) and every entry (`:249`), and `BaseTask.getCurrentTransaction` (`:234`) a `Thread` on every call.

## The gap ledger

**Two appends to existing rows.** Both rows carry a clause about `atomic` on which this rung bears, and both clauses were established with a *local* variable, so neither is wrong — each needs the scope it was measured at.

Row 59 (section 7, Parallelism and mutation), append to the notes column:

> The "`atomic do … end` is correct" clause was measured with a local variable (`matrix-ad-probes/p11.fss:46-50` declares `var acc` inside `run`) and was false for a variable declared at the top level of a component on the compiled path until the repair batch's R1: such a variable was read and written outside the transaction, so `atomic` lost updates there too (`compiler_tests/AtomicTopLevelVar`, 37826 of 40000 with `FORTRESS_THREADS` unset on `49ee5e91`; exact at one thread, which is what the gate runs at).

Row 70 (section 10, Bytecode-compiler path), append to the notes column:

> The "including … `atomic`" clause was measured with local variables (`compiler-probes/p12.fss`, `p13.fss` declare `var acc` inside a function) and did not extend to a variable declared at the top level of a component until R1 of the repair batch; the compiled path's `atomic` is now correct for both — in a function body or a loop body. As the trailing expression of a `do … also` arm the class does not verify at all (row 322), and a Fortress exception thrown out of an `atomic` block leaves the block's writes visible (row 324).

**A third append, to row 302** (section 9), which this round extends:

> The `inATransaction` guard this row recommended and rung 0 applied (`BaseTask.java:248`) was one of **twenty-three** `debug(` call sites in the two transaction runtime files — fourteen in `Transaction.java`, nine in `BaseTask.java` — and the only one that tested the flag before building its argument. R1's repair round of 2026-09-19 guarded the other twenty-two. The sites on the per-access transactional path were `Transaction.java:162` and `:166` (every read), `:227` (every write), `:232` and `:249` (every commit, the first rendering both hash tables whole) and `BaseTask.java:234`; nine of `Transaction.java`'s sites stringify a Fortress value and were also a crash for a value without its own `asString` (row 321).

**Four new rows**, proposed for section 10 (Bytecode-compiler path) after row 318, numbered 319-324 if R2 proposes none. Rows 319 and 320 are as R1 first offered them, except that row 320's three code citations are moved to `HEAD` numbering, where R1's pre-pass insertion moved `forVarRef` down. Row 324 is not in the judge's instruction list: a probe this round added to replace a speculation with a measurement found it, and the brief's fourth case requires the row.

> | 319 | a **mutable field of an object is outside the transaction on the compiled path**: `VarCodeGen.MutableFieldVar` reads with a bare `GETFIELD` and writes with a bare `PUTFIELD` on a non-volatile field (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/VarCodeGen.java:202-231`), so `atomic do n := n + 1 end` on a field loses updates above one thread while the same program is exact under `walk`, whose `ReferenceCell` holds fields and variables alike (`interpreter/env/ReferenceCell.java:26-28`). The fix is the one R1 applied to variables — the field holds a `MutableFValue` and the accesses route through `Transaction.TXRead`/`TXWrite` — and it was deliberately not taken in R1 because `MutableFieldVar` is constructed for *every* `VarDecl` field of an object, mutable or not (`CodeGen.java:4323-4342`, under the team's "TODO need to spot for 'final' fields. Right now we assume mutable, not final"), so the same edit changes the representation of every compiled object's fields and pays a cell per field until that TODO is closed. | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap | `basic/expressions/atomic.tex:38-42`, `:65-67`; `basic/memory-model.tex:69-75` | `compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/P10Field.fss` | ours | Compiled at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`: 34481, 35424, 37726, 37831 and 38910 of 40000 across five runs, on the base tree and on the repaired one alike; exact at one thread; exact under `walk` at one and at four (`probes/walk-differential.txt`). |

> | 320 | a **variable declared at the top level of a component and exported through an api does not link on the compiled path**, whether mutable or immutable: the importing component resolves the name to a singleton class in the *api's* namespace, which no component emits, and the run dies with `NoClassDefFoundError: P8Api$shared` from `Resource not found : P8Api$shared.class`. The reading side is `CodeGen.forVarRef`'s fresh-import path (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:5952-5970`, entered at the `debug("forVarRef fresh import ", v)` of `:5957`), which builds the class name with `NamingCzar.jvmClassForToplevelDecl(id, packageAndClassName)` on the importing component's own package name (`:5966`) and hands it to a plain `StaticBinding` (`:5967`); the writing side emits the class under the *declaring* component's name (`forVarDeclPrePass:5923`). | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap | `basic/components/source-code.tex:332-343` (an api's top-level variable declaration is satisfied by the component's, with the same mutability) and `basic/components/initialization.tex:15-17,29-30` | `compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/P8Api.fsi`+`P8Lib.fss`+`P8Main.fss` (mutable) and `P9*` (immutable, the control) | ours | Both fail identically before and after R1, so mutability is not the cause and R1's change of the field's descriptor did not regress it. Compiles clean; fails at run time. |

> | 321 | **an object or trait value with no `asString` of its own cannot be rendered on the compiled path: it recurses until the stack overflows.** `FValue.toString` is `this.asString().toString()` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/runtimeValues/FValue.java:25-27`); `trait Object`'s default is `getter asString(): String = jAsString(self)` (`ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fss:338`); `jAsString` is bound to `stringOps.asString` (`:270`); and that helper is `return a.toString()` under the team's own `// this can't be right! DRC` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/stringOps.java:38-40`). Three ways in, all pre-existing: user code that stringifies such a value (`println(Box(1).asString)`); every Fortress `throw` of such an object, because `FException`'s constructor builds its `java.lang.Error` message with `v.asString()` (`runtimeValues/FException.java:22-23`); and, until R1's repair round guarded them, the transaction runtime's eagerly built debug arguments (which is how a *local* mutable variable of trait type inside `atomic` died on `49ee5e91`, and how R1's landed tree briefly killed the top-level case too). | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap | — the prose chapters are **silent**: `grep -rn asString Specification/basic Specification/basic-lib` finds nothing, so what such a value should render as is an open language decision. The team's own commented-out alternative is at `stringOps.java:39` (`return "<" + a.getClass() + ">"`). | `compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/skeptic/SK27DefaultAsString.fss` (+ `sk27-default-asstring.txt`), `SK3Throw.fss` (+ `sk3-recursion-entry.txt`), `SK20LocalTrait.fss` (+ `skeptic-basetree.txt:24-25`), `SK24TraitAsString.fss` (the control: the same program with an `asString` works) | ours | `walk` answers `Box` — the object's own name — for the same expression, so the interpreter already has a rendering and the compiled path has none. **Three candidate fixes, not chosen by this batch**: the team's class-name line at `stringOps.java:39`; a default `asString` at `CompilerBuiltin.fss:338` that does not go through `jAsString`; or an `FValue.toString` that does not call `asString`. The choice decides what every `println` of an unadorned object prints, so it is Pavol's. |

> | 322 | **`atomic` as the trailing expression of a `do … also` arm produces a class that does not verify**: `java.lang.VerifyError: Inconsistent stackmap frames at branch target 5`, with a top-level variable, with a local variable and one nesting level deeper, on the base tree and on the repaired one alike. `CodeGen.generateTaskCompute` loads `this` and leaves it on the operand stack across the arm's body so that the result can be stored with a `PUTFIELD` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/codegen/CodeGen.java:4733-4738`, body at `:4740`, `PUTFIELD` at `:4741`), while `CodeGen.forAtomicBlock` makes `startOver` the first label of the region (`:1737`) and branches back to it from the handler (`:1753`), where the JVM has cleared the stack to the exception and the `POP` at `:1747` empties it. The general statement: `forAtomicBlock` is correct only when the operand stack is empty at its entry, so `atomic` cannot appear as a task body's trailing expression, nor — by the same mechanism — as any argument but the first of a call. The fix is to generate the body first and then `ALOAD this; SWAP` before the `PUTFIELD`, the trick `VarCodeGen.MutableFieldVar.assignValue` already uses for the same reason (`VarCodeGen.java:218-220`). | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap | `basic/expressions/also.tex:17-20` (each `also` block runs in a separate implicit thread) with `basic/expressions/atomic.tex:96-107` (the chapter's own worked example of `atomic` inside implicit threads); `:77-81` for the nested case | `compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/skeptic/SK12ArmAtomic.fss` (top-level), `SK13LocalArmAtomic.fss` (local, the control that places it outside R1), `SK7TaskNest.fss` and `SK14LocalTaskNest.fss` (one level deeper); disassembly in `sk13-verifyerror.txt`; rows on both trees in `skeptic-basetree.txt:29-31,93-95` and `skeptic-controls-after-guard.txt` | ours | `walk` runs all four correctly (`g = 3`, `g = 43`). This bounds R1's own claim: `atomic` on a top-level mutable variable works in a function body or a loop body, not as a `do … also` arm's trailing expression. |

> | 323 | **`walk` rejects a singleton object's field initializer that reads a top-level *mutable* variable declared later in the component**, which the compiled path runs correctly: `ProgramError: Attempt to find type of uninitialized variable: thunk (IntLiteralExpr …)` at the field's own line, while the compiled path prints the right answers on the base tree and the repaired one alike. The reference is licensed by the specification, so this is a defect of the interpreter. Narrowed by one control: with the later variable *immutable* (`d: ZZ32 = 5` in place of `d: ZZ32 := 5`) `walk` accepts the same program, and `tests/InitOrderWithMutable.fss` shows `walk` accepts a *top-level* initializer reading a later mutable variable — so the failure is specific to a singleton object field initializer reading a later mutable variable. | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap (walk interpreter) | `basic/variables.tex:122-123` — "The initializer expressions of top-level variable declarations can refer to variables declared later in textual order" — with `basic/components/initialization.tex:15-17,29-30` (top-level variables and singleton object fields are initialized before their use, in no prescribed textual order) and `basic/objects.tex:202-203` (singleton initialization is nondeterministic) | `compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/skeptic/SK5InitFwd.fss` and `SK26InitFwdImmutable.fss` (the control); captures in `skeptic-differential-after-guard.txt` and `sk26-initfwd-immutable.txt` | ours | Compiled, both trees: `a = 11 b = 10 c = 12 Holder.f = 5 d = 5`. Both citations hold at those lines; what a probe would still have to confirm is that this, rather than a plain committed write, is the route by which the value survives. The fix is a second handler, or a `finally`, that cleans the transaction up on any abrupt completion; `atomic.tex:59-62`'s rule that writes *are* retained for an `exit` to an enclosing `label` means the two cases must be distinguished rather than merged. | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | implementation gap | `basic/expressions/atomic.tex:65-67` — "Any variable reverts to the value it held before evaluation of the `atomic` expression began" — with `:59-62` for the `exit` case the fix must not break | `compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/probes/skeptic/SK28ThrowAsString.fss` (top-level) and `SK29ThrowLocalAsString.fss` (local, the control); captures `sk28-throw-asstring.txt`, `sk29-throw-local-asstring.txt`; and `probes/skeptic/SQ7ObjThrow.fss` (object type), `SQ6OrphanTx.fss` (a second implicit thread), capture `skeptic2-sq6-sq7.txt` | ours | The wrong answer is measured on the repaired tree only: on the base tree the same programs are unrunnable for an unrelated reason (row 321 — `SK3Throw` and `SK19ThrowLocal` overflow because the thrown object has no `asString`), and the local control shows the defect is in `forAtomicBlock`, which R1 does not touch. The answer 7 is wrong before the repair too, by a simpler route: the write went straight to the static field. The mechanism in the claim column is derived from the two code sites cited there and is the half a probe would still confirm. ## The handover state line

> R1 of the repair batch is on `wip/repair-r1-atomic-static` (base `49ee5e91`), refused once by its skeptic and repaired in the same worktree: a top-level mutable variable is now in the transaction on the compiled path, the cell's payload is widened to `fortress.AnyType.Any`, the top-level variable bindings are registered before any initializer is generated, and all twenty-two eagerly built debug arguments in `runtimeSystem/Transaction.java` and `BaseTask.java` are guarded with `if (debug)` — the last of these because routing accesses through the transaction had turned a working program into a `StackOverflowError` for any value whose type has no `asString` of its own. Three gated tests in `compiler_tests/`: `MutableTopLevelVarInLoop` and `AtomicTopLevelObjectVar`, both deterministic and both failing at one thread on the tree each guards, and `AtomicTopLevelVar` under contention. Six verified ledger rows are owed by this rung and are written out in `explorations/compile-ladder/repair-r1-atomic-static/record.md`: the mutable object field inside `atomic`, a top-level variable exported through an api, the `asString` cycle (with three candidate fixes and a silent specification — a decision for Pavol), `atomic` as a `do … also` arm's trailing expression, `walk` rejecting a singleton field initializer that reads a later mutable top-level variable, and a Fortress exception thrown out of an `atomic` block leaving its writes visible. The batch's gate (`ant testFast` and `ant testSystem`, both required — `REPAIR-BATCH.md`, "The gate is the full pair") has not been run: it is the coordinator's, once, after the merge with R2. R2 touches neither runtime file (`git diff --stat 49ee5e91 origin/wip/repair-r2-literal-wrap -- ProjectFortress/src`: `CodeGen.java`, `FIntLiteral.java`, `Library/CompilerLibrary.fss`), so the two rungs' edits do not overlap outside `CodeGen.java`, where they are 2,000 lines apart.

## One decision about the gate, for Pavol rather than for this rung

Under `experiment/env.sh:6` every gate run gives `compiler_tests` one worker, so a concurrent test there cannot fail and `AtomicTopLevelVar` passes vacuously. The candidates are to leave it — the discipline holds, because both of R1's other tests fail at one thread — or to set a thread count for `fastTrack` in `build.xml:927-953`, whose cost is nondeterminism across every compiled test program and which `iteration-cost.md:126` already prices as "not recommended" for a different reason. Not decided here.

# Rung F: the record

## FACTS.md

Two lines. The first is the rung; the second is a fact it established on the way and that the next native-helper rung will want.

> **Rung F of climb batch 1, the thirteen functional methods of `trait RR64`, landed** (2026-09-19, `compile-ladder/rung-rr64-functions/REPORT.md`): thirteen declarations in `ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:439-451` and thirteen one-line bodies in `.fss:911-923` — `sin`, `cos`, `tan`, `asin`, `acos`, `atan`, `atan2(self, x:RR64)`, `log` and `exp` returning `RR64`, `floor` and `ceiling` returning `RR64`, `truncate` and `round` returning `ZZ64` — over eleven new static methods in the team's own `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleDoubleArith.java:92-134` bound in the `simpleDoubleArith` `import java` block at `.fss:215-225`; `ant compileAll` was needed and the five library jars rebuilt after it, with `default_repository/caches/nativewrapper_cache` deleted first. `floor` and `ceiling` uncomment the team's own draft at `.fsi:439-440` unchanged, and the `RR64` return type is theirs: the specification gives the four rounding methods a ℤ result (`Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:457-462`) but also makes each method and its enclosing operator the same operation (`:464`, `:467`, "likewise the enclosing operator"), and the compiler prelude's two brackets were already declared `RR64` (`.fsi:437-438`), which a rung may not change. **`round` is `(long) Math.rint(a)` and not `Math.round`**: an exact half goes to the even integer, which is what `numbers.tex:470-472` requires and what the team's own ℚ body computes in Fortress (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:589`), where the interpreter's `Float$Round` is `Math.round` and answers `3` for `round(2.5)` (ledger row 329). `library_tests/RR64FunctionsRungF` + `.test` passes — 44 assertions, the nine transcendentals pinned by identities rather than against printed decimals, all four half-way cases of `round`, and `exp` and `log` used as function values both bound and passed. Of the seven-file ladder subset all seven clear every one of the thirteen names, three advance disambiguate → typecheck (`buffons`, `roundBug`, `juxtTwice`), `oprTests` advances into typecheck and crashes there on the catalogued array-literal defect at `Misc.scala:876`, and `realArith`, `testRR32` and `RationalTest` keep their phase with 17, 6 and 48 fewer errors; nothing moved down and **the ladder's pass count does not move**, because none of the seven reaches a run. The first blocker of three of them is now one missing line of prelude, `coerce(x: IntLiteral)` on `trait RR64` (`.fsi:414-415` has `FloatLiteral` and `RR32` and not `IntLiteral`), which makes `random(2.0) - 1`, `SQRT(a^2+b^2)` on `ZZ32` and `4.5 / 2` all fail to check; the other is the ten IEEE directed-rounding operators. Ledger rows 329 and 330.

> **A native helper that takes a `double` and returns a `long` needs no `NamingCzar` clause**, and rung F's `doubleTruncate` and `doubleRound` are the first two in the tree (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/nativeHelpers/simpleDoubleArith.java:128-134`). The foreign-Java route maps JVM primitives through `NamingCzar`'s own table — `s(Type.LONG_TYPE, fortLib, "ZZ64")` and `s(Type.DOUBLE_TYPE, fortLib, "RR64")`, `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:441-446` — and the chain of else-ifs at `:328-350` that rung 7 had to extend is reached only by a helper dealing in a *Fortress* type. So the criterion for "new file or the team's file" is that one: a helper over primitives belongs in the existing `simple*Arith.java` of its type, a helper over a Fortress value needs its own file and its own clause.

## The gap ledger

**Two new rows**, proposed for the sections named, numbered 329 and 330 if no earlier rung of the batch proposes any.

Row 329, section 8 (the walk interpreter's own defects) — the interpreter's `round` on a float:

> | 329 | **the interpreter's `round` sends an exact half to the wrong integer on a float**: `Float$Round` is `Math.round(x)` (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/interpreter/glue/prim/Float.java:382-385`), which rounds a half toward positive infinity, where `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:470-472` requires "whichever of the two integers is **even**". `walk` answers `round(2.5) = 3` and `round(-3.5) = -3` where the specification requires `2` and `-4`; it is right at `3.5` and `-2.5` only because half-up and half-to-even coincide there. The interpreter contradicts **itself** as well as the specification: `trait QQ`'s `round` is a hand-written round-half-to-even body in Fortress — `round(self): ZZ = do x = self + 1/2; z = floor(x); if z = x AND odd z then z-1 else z end end` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:589`) — and the gated interpreter test `ProjectFortress/tests/RationalTest.fss:428` asserts `round(15/6) = 2`, that is `round(2.5) = 2`, on ℚ. The compiled path was given the specification's rule by rung F of climb batch 1, so the two paths now disagree at `2.5` and at `-3.5`. | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library bug (walk interpreter) | `basic-lib/numbers.tex:470-472` | `compile-ladder/rung-rr64-functions/probes/RoundHalfWalkProbe.fss` + `.out` (walk) against `RoundHalfCompiledProbe.fss` + `.out` (compiled), the same ten values built the same way; `ProjectFortress/library_tests/RR64FunctionsRungF.fss:98-101` pins the compiled side | ours (climb batch 1, rung F) | **The fix is one token**: `Math.round(x)` → `(long) Math.rint(x)` at `Float.java:384`, which is what rung F's `simpleDoubleArith.doubleRound` does (`:132-134`). > | 330 | **`floor` and `ceiling` on the float types return a float where the specification returns an integer, and the named method and the enclosing operator do not agree across the two paths**: `Specification/basic-lib/numbers.tex:457-462` declares `floor`, `⌊…⌋`, `ceiling`, `⌈…⌉`, `round` and `truncate` all returning ℤ, and `:464` and `:467` make each method and its enclosing operator the same operation ("likewise the enclosing operator"). So three of the four spellings hand back a float, and `⌊x⌋` has a different type on the two paths: `walk` and the compiled path both print `floor(-2.5) = -3.0`, while `⌊-2.5⌋` is a `ZZ64` under `walk` and an `RR64` compiled. | NEGATIVE-VERIFIED | library gap vs spec | `basic-lib/numbers.tex:457-462`, `:464-468` | `compile-ladder/rung-rr64-functions/probes/RoundHalfWalkProbe.out` and `RoundHalfCompiledProbe.out`; `ProjectFortress/library_tests/RR64FunctionsRungF.fss:90-93` asserts that the method and the bracket agree on the compiled path | ours (climb batch 1, rung F) | **The fix is an api change on both paths** and is one of the two stops `CLIMB-BATCH-1.md` reserves, which is why rung F copied the team's commented-out `ceiling(self):RR64` / `floor(self):RR64` (`CompilerBuiltin.fsi:439-440` before the edit) rather than declaring the methods at `ZZ64` and leaving one trait in which `floor(x)` and `⌊x⌋` have different types.
